newsitem.title: INDIA: India to raise urea fertiliser price by 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: India to raise urea fertiliser price by 10 pct.

text.p: The Indian government has decided to raise the price of urea fertiliser by about 10 percent to 3,660 rupees per tonne, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.
The current price of urea fertiliser is 3,320 rupees per tonne, the spokesman told reporters.
He said the price increase would be announced on the floor of parliament after it reconvenes on Thursday.
The government will save some 7.5 billion rupees a year in subsidy costs after the price increase, he said.
India consumed 21.1 million tonnes of fertiliser in 1996/97 (April-March), the spokesman said.
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has decided to raise the concession, or subsidy, on a range of other fertilisers, the spokesman said.
The concession on di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) fertiliser will be raised to 4,000 rupees per tonne from 3,000, he said.
The concession on muriate of potash (MOP) fertiliser will be increased to 2,000 rupees per tonne from 1,500.
The concession on complex fertilisers will be raised to 3,937 rupees per tonne from 1,304.
The concession on single super phosphate (SSP) will be increased to 600 rupees per tonne from 500, he said.
